provenance.paper_title: 3D-Mem: 3D Scene Memory for Embodied Exploration and Reasoning

latest_version.version_label: arXiv current version served on review date

evidence.paraphrase: Selected raw multi-view RGB-D observations are retained as Memory Snapshots to preserve object and background detail.

evidence.section: Full paper: 10.1. Implementation Details for A-EQA
evidence.paraphrase: Frontier Snapshots retain an image, navigable location, and the unexplored region it represents, and are directly supplied to the VLM.
Objects with categories and 3D locations are assigned to co-visible image snapshots; each snapshot links an object cluster to an observation.

evidence.section: Full paper: 3.2.3. Memory Retrieval with Prefiltering
evidence.paraphrase: A VLM ranks object categories for the instruction and filters snapshots that contain none of the selected categories.

At every exploration step, fixed procedures add detected objects, recluster affected snapshots, and add, modify, or remove frontier snapshots. For 3D-Mem, this specifically supports fixed-rule insertion or replacement of Memory Snapshots and Frontier Snapshots.

Snapshots that select the same frame candidate are merged after object clustering to maintain a compact set. For 3D-Mem, this specifically supports merging or deduplication of overlapping entries of Memory Snapshots and Frontier Snapshots.

derived.hybrid_relation: Structured object/frontier state remains linked to retained snapshot images that the VLM directly inspects.

adjudication_notes: Strict-tier full-paper review (PDF p. 4): During inference, the operative memory component (Memory Snapshots and Frontier Snapshots) changes through fixed-rule insertion or replacement, merging or deduplication of overlapping entries; the governing policy remains fixed, and any learning reported by the paper occurs before deployment. Training-time learning, when present, was not counted as T3.
